title: Strategy Optimization and Forward Analysis (Part 1): The Pardo Method — A Basic Model

for: BUY SIGNAL: Bar OPEN price > UPPER Envelopes band AND OPEN[0] > OPEN[1] AND OPEN[0] > MAX(High[2..N])
SELL SIGNAL: Bar OPEN price < LOWER Envelopes band AND OPEN[0] < OPEN[1] AND OPEN[0] < MIN(Low[2..N])
The indicator first checks the price's position relative to the channel: if ABOVE upper band → check BUY conditions; if BELOW lower band → check SELL conditions; if INSIDE → NO signals
All conditions are checked on the current bar '0' (candlestick) — this ensures an immediate response to a trading signal
Mathematical formula for trading signals explicitly given: buy = Open[0] > Open[1] AND Open[0] > MAX(High[2..N]) AND Open[0] > UpperEnvelopes

against: In the PardoSystem indicator, the Pardo extremum calculation uses future bars: 'MAX(High[bar+2] ... High[bar+InpLookbackBars])' — i.e., it accesses high[bar+2], high[bar+3], ..., up to high[bar+InpLookbackBars], where bar is the current (0-indexed) bar under evaluation. This is forward-looking: for bar 0, it reads High[2], High[3], ..., High[InpLookbackBars], which are bars *after* the current bar — violating causality. The signal is computed on bar 0 but depends on prices from bars that have not yet closed (and may not even have formed). This is pernicious because the logic explicitly requires 'lookahead' beyond the current bar — not just a rolling window over past bars. The article states: 'MAX(High[2..N])' and in OnCalculate(): 'MAX(High[bar+2] ... High[bar+InpLookbackBars])'. This is a textbook case of using future data — a fatal lookahead violation (Port 1).

In Breakout_Bounce EA, daily levels are calculated via CopyHigh(_Symbol, PERIOD_D1, 1, InpDayPeriod, highArray), i.e., it reads D1 bars starting from index 1 (yesterday’s D1 bar) up to InpDayPeriod bars back. However, the EA runs on lower timeframes (e.g., M1, H1), and the condition 'Ask > DayHighLevel' is evaluated on the *current tick* — but DayHighLevel is computed from fully closed D1 bars only. That part is valid. However, the critical flaw is in the *timing of level recalculation*: CalculateDailyLevels() checks 'if (dayLevelsDate == today && dayHighLevel > 0 && dayLowLevel > 0) return true', where 'today = iTime(_Symbol, PERIOD_D1, 0)' — i.e., the open time of the *current, still-forming* D1 bar. But the D1 bar at index 0 is not closed — its high/low is undefined or volatile. Yet the code assumes 'today' identifies a completed day. Worse: the CopyHigh call uses shift=1 (i.e., starts from yesterday’s closed D1 bar), which is correct — so this part is *not* lookahead. So no Port 1 here. But the PardoSystem flaw stands alone.

The PardoSystem's extremum logic cannot be rewritten using only past bars without breaking the idea: the article defines it as 'MAX(High[2..N])' relative to the *current bar*, and the code implements exactly that — accessing indices > bar. Replacing with MAX(High[0..N-2]) would invert the logic (past extremum, not future extremum) and destroy the stated 'local extremum breakout' meaning. Thus, the idea fundamentally relies on non-causal access — making it unfalsifiable in real-time trading (Port 1).
non_fatal: No spread or commission modeling in examples
No robustness analysis across instruments or brokers
No discussion of parameter sensitivity beyond plateau search
No statistical significance testing of results

judge.reject_reason: Фатальный порок: использование будущих цен в правиле входа. В индикаторе PardoSystem при расчёте сигнала на баре с индексом 'bar' выполняется обращение к high[bar+2], high[bar+3], ..., high[bar+InpLookbackBars], то есть к ценам баров, следующих *после* текущего (бар 0). Это заглядывание вперёд (lookahead), поскольку на момент открытия бара 0 бары с индексами > 0 ещё не закрыты и их High не определены. Статья прямо указывает на это: 'MAX(High[2..N])' и в коде — 'MAX(High[bar+2] ... High[bar+InpLookbackBars])'. Такое правило неприменимо в реальной торговле и не может быть исправлено сдвигом на закрытые бары без изменения самой логики (например, замена на MAX(High[0..N-2]) превратит 'локальный экстремум пробоя' в 'пробой прошлого экстремума', что противоречит описанию). Это нарушение причинности — фатальный порок, дающий основание для REJECT.

repaint.note: Расчёт MAX(High[bar+2]..High[bar+N]) использует цены будущих баров, недоступных на момент формирования сигнала на bar 0

judge.summary: Статья описывает методологию тестирования торговых стратегий и представляет два EA: PardoSystem и Breakout_Bounce. Однако в реализации PardoSystem обнаружен фатальный порок — сигнал рассчитывается с использованием цен будущих баров (High[bar+2..bar+N]), что делает правило неприменимым в реальной торговле. Этот порок неустраним без изменения сути стратегии и является достаточным основанием для отказа.
